title: README: architecture brought up to date, with a diagram
lede: No runtime code changes. The README's Architecture section hadn't changed since #12. It now covers `commands.ts` and the ui store, the Trash zone in the move kind, a Click starting Editing, the keyboard, and the re-render tests. The prose is now key ideas with bullets under a Mermaid overview. This walkthrough checks the new claims against the code.

files.question: How is the app put together?
files.summary: A diagram of the UI layer and the pure core, then four key ideas and Testing.
files.owns: The reviewer's first view of the architecture.
files.tested: Prettier only. The diagram is drawn by GitHub, not checked in CI.

files.question: Where do the rules that span both stores live?
files.summary: Unchanged. Create, delete, recolour, pick a colour, commit a Drag, Undo.
files.owns: Rules that touch both the notes and the ui store.

files.question: How does a drop on the Trash zone become a delete?
files.summary: Unchanged. The move kind's `commit` returns a delete when the pointer is inside the zone.
files.owns: What each Drag kind shows and saves.

files.question: Why does a change of Editing re-render only two Notes?
files.summary: Unchanged. `useIsEditing` gives each Note a boolean.
files.owns: The hooks components read the stores through.
files.never: Changes value, so reading it never renders.

scenarios.name: A reviewer reads the Architecture section

steps.title: The diagram gives the overview
steps.explain: React components on one side, the pure core on the other. Solid arrows are calls, dotted arrows are selector subscriptions. It wasn't previewed locally: check that it draws on the PR's file view.

steps.title: A drop on the Trash zone is a delete from the move kind
steps.explain: The README says the Trash zone belongs to the move kind. The pointer, not the Note's rect, must be inside the zone.

steps.title: That delete goes through commands, so it gets Undo
steps.explain: A Drag's commit passes through `commit`, which sends a delete to `deleteNote`. That ends Editing and records the Note for Undo, the same as the ×.

steps.title: A change of Editing re-renders only two Notes
steps.explain: Each Note subscribes to a boolean, not to `editingId`, so only the Notes whose boolean flips re-render.

notes.title: Claims checked against the tests
notes.detail: The Testing paragraph lists the `<Profiler>` tests found in the browser tests: move, resize, setText, setColour, delete and the change of Editing.
